title: fix(driver-sql): the boot drift line for an organization_id drop names the ownership ceremony on an uncertified database
body:
Fixes #24956

Clause-②: no (operator log line text only)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

`SqlDriver`'s boot reconcile (`reconcileAndWarnDrift`) logs each drift entry as `[schema-drift] MESSAGE`. When an entry is an `organization_id` `drop_column`, it now asks the driver's own reader, `isTenantKeyCertified()`, once per table and only when such a line is about to print. The reader goes through the engine-handed resolver over `isOrganizationOwnershipCertified()`: a birth marker, or a ceremony marker of the current shape generation. No second list is involved.

- **Not certified:** the line keeps the finding (`driftFindingWithoutRemedy`). It replaces the `--allow-destructive` sentence with PR #24954's vocabulary for the same entry: `— a drop the organization-ownership ceremony owns, and it has not verified on this database: run "os migrate organization-ownership", which drops it itself.`
- **Certified, or any other column or drift kind:** the line is the differ's message, byte for byte.
- **Unchanged:** what the boot applies or skips, the `driftWarned` de-duplication, and the drop gate (`packages/cli`).

Files: `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts` adds `isCeremonyOwnedColumnDrop` and `ceremonyOwnedDropFinding`. They are module exports only and are not added to the package's `index.ts`, so the public surface does not change. `sql-driver.ts` adds the branch. There is one new test file and a `patch` changeset.

## Measured: a real `create-objectstack@17.7.0` SQLite database, `OS_AUTH_SECRET` set

The fixture was scaffolded with `npx create-objectstack@17.7.0`; it ran on `@objectstack/*@17.7.0` and booted once with `objectstack dev -d file:./v17.db`. It carries 43 tables with an `organization_id` column. Each door ran on a fresh copy, through this tree's CLI (`packages/cli/bin/run.js`) and a copy of the scaffold's app with `engines.protocol` set to `^18`.

| door | `main` `82cfaf792` | this branch `bdd1ac563` |
|---|---|---|
| `os serve` | exit 1 (boot guard refusal); 28 `[schema-drift]` lines, **9** `organization_id` drop lines naming `--allow-destructive` | exit 1 (same refusal); 28 lines, **0** naming `--allow-destructive` for `organization_id`, 9 naming `os migrate organization-ownership` |
| `os migrate apply --yes` | exit 0; 28 lines, **9** as above | exit 0; 28 lines, **0** as above, 9 naming the ceremony |
| `os migrate plan` | exit 0; no `[schema-drift]` lines (its own renderer already names the ceremony, PR #24954) | unchanged |
| `os migrate apply --yes --allow-destructive` (main) | exit 1, refused by the drop gate; `sys_job.organization_id` still present | not re-run (the gate is untouched) |

The 9 tables are `sys_metadata`, `sys_metadata_history`, `sys_metadata_commit`, `sys_migration`, `sys_migration_journal`, `sys_secret`, `sys_flow_credential`, `sys_job` and `sys_job_queue`. The card counted 22 lines at `003e41ab5`; today's `main` prints 28. On both `serve` and `apply --yes`, the 19 other drift lines are identical between `main` and this branch (`diff` empty).

**Certified control.** A fresh database from this branch (birth marker `adr-0131-organization-ownership` verified), plus a hand-added `sys_user.organization_id` column. Its boot prints `[schema-drift] sys_user.organization_id: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.`, unchanged. The resolver answers "certified" at boot time.

**The fork the dispatch named did not occur.** The driver's reader answers "not certified" for this card's population. That is the same reading the boot's `recreate_index` lines already print ("This database is not certified for the organization-ownership shape").

## Pins and ablation

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ceremony-owned-drop-line.test.ts` runs on real SQLite through `initObjects`, with a 17.x-shaped table:

1. not certified (the resolver answers no): the `organization_id` line names `"os migrate organization-ownership"` and never `--allow-destructive`; the reader is asked once;
2. no resolver handed over: the same line;
3. certified: the line equals the differ's message exactly;
4. control, not certified: an orphaned `legacy_code` drop is unchanged (exact);
5. control, not certified: a `tighten_not_null` is unchanged (exact);
6. a table with no `organization_id` drop never asks the reader.

**Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`): the guard was prefixed with `false &&`, so the anchor went from 1 hit to 0 and the blob from `24448296bf26` to `cb74d2820589`. Pins 1 and 2 went red; pins 3 to 6 stayed green (2 failed, 4 passed). After restore the blob equals HEAD (`24448296bf26`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The test imports `./sql-driver.js` from `src`, so no `dist` preflight applies.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql typecheck`: exit 0. The new test file is in the program (`--listFiles` count 1).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql test`: exit 0, `Test Files 231 passed | 12 skipped (243)`, `Tests 3748 passed | 212 skipped (3960)`. This is on the merged head `970f966b9`, and again before the merge. It ran SQLite only; live PG and MySQL are left to CI.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: exit 0, `323 passed (323)` files, `4769 passed` tests (at `bdd1ac563`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project integration --maxWorkers=2`: exit 0, `166 passed | 1 skipped (167)` files, `1447 passed | 9 skipped` tests (at `bdd1ac563`). It ran locally because the diff touches the driver boot path.
- After merging `origin/main` (`6251f5905`): `pnpm exec turbo run build --concurrency=2` exit 0 (77/77 tasks), then typecheck and the driver-sql suite as above.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `970f966b9` derived 70 commands, and all 70 exit 0. The first run, at `bdd1ac563`, had `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, unbuilt packages); it exited 0 after the full build. `--ran`: `70 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs.** No page under `content/docs/**` quotes the boot line. The `destructive` row of `deployment/cli.mdx`'s drift table and its `--allow-destructive` refusals list stay true, so I found no page this change falsifies.
- **The column name.** `organization_id` is spelled once in `schema-drift.ts` (`CEREMONY_OWNED_DROP_COLUMN`). That matches the CLI gate's `ORGANIZATION_COLUMN`. It names the ceremony's column, not a list of tables. The decision to hold comes from `isTenantKeyCertified()` alone.
- **A resolver that throws.** It reads "not certified", and `isTenantKeyCertified()` logs its existing one-time warning. That warning's wording is about index comparison. A database whose ledger read fails, and which has an `organization_id` drop, would now see it printed. Before, it printed only with a COALESCE-keyed index.
- **Orphaned indexes keyed on `organization_id`** (for example `idx_sys_metadata_org_type`, a `drop_index`) still name `--allow-destructive` on this database, at boot and in `os migrate plan`. The CLI gate judges `drop_column` only, so those lines are not the ceremony's under today's gate. They are out of this card's scope and noted only.
- **18.0-born databases** (#24638's `tenant: false` case) are certified by their birth marker, and their line is unchanged. #24638 is not addressed here.
